assessment.rationale: No reliable system forecasts earthquakes days ahead with location and size, so the Main KPI of 1 reliable earthquake forecast system is unmet. The USGS states that no scientist has ever predicted a major earthquake and that only long-term probabilities can be calculated (https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/can-you-predict-earthquakes). Operational tools are probabilistic aftershock forecasts issued after a mainshock (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/data/oaf/schedule.php) and seconds-scale ShakeAlert warnings. The best prospective result found, a UT Austin AI that called 70 percent of quakes a week ahead within about 200 miles in a seven-month China trial, had eight false alarms and its authors say it is not close to global use (https://news.utexas.edu/2023/10/05/ai-driven-earthquake-forecasting-shows-promise-in-trials/). Honest limit: open testing infrastructure already exists (pyCSEP and a decade of prospective next-day forecasts, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12391313/); a task must beat those benchmarks prospectively, and deterministic prediction may be physically impossible.

additionalSearches.query: deterministic earthquake prediction not possible USGS statement short-term forecast
additionalSearches.finding: USGS: neither the USGS nor any scientist has predicted a major earthquake; only probabilities over years can be given.

additionalSearches.query: USGS operational aftershock forecasting OAF probabilistic forecast
additionalSearches.finding: USGS publishes automated probabilistic aftershock forecasts starting about 30 minutes after a mainshock; forecasts, not predictions of new mainshocks.

additionalSearches.query: machine learning earthquake prediction days ahead location magnitude trial 2023 China UT Austin AI 70%
additionalSearches.finding: UT Austin AI predicted 70 percent of quakes a week ahead in a 7-month China trial, 1 miss and 8 false warnings; not generalised.

additionalSearches.query: CSEP Collaboratory Study of Earthquake Predictability forecast testing results open source pyCSEP
additionalSearches.finding: CSEP ran 25 next-day models prospectively for 10 years in California; data on Zenodo and pyCSEP is open source for testing forecasts.
